rules: Starting capital $50,000. Individual US stocks only: no ETFs, shorting, options or margin.
Max 20% of the book in one stock.
Target 5-15% cash in normal times; up to 40% while waiting on a clear catalyst.
Decisions are made after the close and filled at the next trading day's opening price. No trading at a price already seen.
Daily review is light: mark prices, check stops, targets, earnings dates and red-flag news. The default outcome is no trade.
New positions are opened mainly in the weekly review (Saturday). At most 3 new positions per week.
Hold each position at least 5 trading days, unless its stop is hit or its thesis breaks on real news.
Every position gets a stop and a target at entry. A close below the stop means exit at the next open, or a written reason to hold.
No new full-size position the day before that company's earnings. Earnings bets are sized at 5% or less, on purpose.

Prices and facts come from primary or established sources (exchange data providers, company filings, Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC). Promotional and AI-prediction sites are ignored. X posts are idea leads only and must be confirmed.
No commissions or slippage are modeled.

watchlist.note: Fiscal Q4 out after the Sep 30 close: revenue $54.2B vs about $51.1B expected, EPS $33.42 vs $31.61, Q1 guide $61.5B vs about $57.0B. Clear beat and raise. Buy only if the Oct 1 session confirms (holds a gap up into the close) rather than fading it.
About 29% below its $495 high and drifting sideways. Forward P/E near 20 is attractive, but wait for the trend to turn before buying.
Up about 29% in September on its AI agent launch. Extended after that run; a pullback toward support would be the entry.

trades.reasoning: Best risk/reward among the AI leaders. Revenue roughly doubled while the stock rose only about 24% this year, so the forward P/E compressed to around 19x, near its lowest in a decade. A record $150B buyback adds a steady bid. Price is just under the $236.54 52-week high with the daily trend intact; a clean break above that level would likely pull in momentum buyers. Also a read-through beneficiary if Micron's results tonight confirm AI memory demand.

trades.reasoning: Replaces the Nasdaq-100 ETF as a direct tech holding. Alphabet sits about 16% below its $408.61 high while earnings per share more than doubled over the past year, leaving it at roughly 17x trailing earnings, cheap for a megacap AI platform. Communication services was one of the stronger groups today, the stock closed up about 1% and traded higher after hours. Analyst consensus is Strong Buy with an average target near $429. trades.exitPlan: Stop at $475 (about 7% down). Target $575, near the consensus target. Earnings around Oct 28.
trades.reasoning: Momentum pick. Microsoft rose about 39% this quarter, on track for its best quarter since 1991, driven by cloud and AI demand, and it closes the quarter only about 7% below its $553.72 high. Piper Sandler just raised its target to $610. Strong trends into a quarter-end tend to carry into the next earnings report, which is the window this trade is built for. What would prove it wrong: a sharp reversal on heavy volume or a cloud growth slowdown in the October report.

trades.exitPlan: Stop at $151 (about 7% down). Target $178, near the $176 high. Earnings Oct 30. Exit fast if a US-Iran deal knocks oil sharply lower.
trades.reasoning: Replaces the energy ETF with the best single name. Oil rose about 12-14% in September on stalled US-Iran talks and tight fuel supplies, and refining margins are very strong. TD Cowen expects Exxon's Q3 to beat consensus on refining strength and raised its target to $180 with a Buy rating. The stock is below its $176.41 high, so there is room to run into the Oct 30 report. It also balances the book: if the war escalates and tech sells off, energy should rise.

snapshots.note: Day one. Stocks faded into the close after a cooler August PCE reading and the S&P 500 finished September with a monthly loss as long-term yields stayed near multi-decade highs; oil sits near $100 with the Iran war in its eighth month. Opened five individual stocks (NVDA, GOOGL, MSFT, XOM, GEV) late in the session, about 65% invested with 35% cash held back; the book is marked at the official closes, slightly below the entry prices. After the bell Micron beat on revenue and EPS and guided Q1 revenue well above expectations, a positive read for AI hardware including NVDA. Watching tomorrow's Micron reaction for a possible entry, and planning ahead for GOOGL, MSFT and GEV reporting around Oct 28 and XOM on Oct 30.
